ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is the midpoint of the diagonal $AC$ of rectangle $ABCD$, and $E$ is a point on $AB$. After folding $\triangle BCE$ along $CE$, point $B$ coincides exactly with point $O$. If $BC = 3$, what is the length of the crease $CE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, we connect $OB$, \\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle, and O is the midpoint of the diagonal AC of rectangle ABCD, \\
it follows that $BO=CO$, and $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, \\
since folding $\triangle BCE$ along CE exactly overlaps point B with point O, \\
it follows that $BC=OC$, and $\angle BCE=\angle OCE$, \\
thus, $OB=OC=BC$, \\
which means $\triangle OBC$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
therefore, $\angle OCB=60^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle BCE=\angle OCE=30^\circ$, \\
In the right triangle $\triangle BCE$, $CE=2EB$, and $CB=3$, \\
$CE^2=BC^2+EB^2$, \\
which implies $CE^2=\left(\frac{1}{2}CE\right)^2+3^2$, \\
solving this gives us $CE=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $O$ is the midpoint of the diagonal $AC$ of rectangle $ABCD$, and $E$ is a point on $AB$. After folding $\triangle BCE$ along $CE$, point $B$ coincides with point $O$. If $BC = 3$, what is the length of the crease $CE$?
raw_record.answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, we connect $OB$. Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle, and $O$ is the midpoint of the diagonal $AC$ of rectangle $ABCD$, it follows that $BO=CO$, and $\angle ABC=90^\circ$. Since folding $\triangle BCE$ along $CE$ exactly overlaps point $B$ with point $O$, it follows that $BC=OC$, and $\angle BCE=\angle OCE$. Thus, $OB=OC=BC$, which means $\triangle OBC$ is an equilateral triangle. Therefore, $\angle OCB=60^\circ$, and $\angle BCE=\angle OCE=30^\circ$. In the right triangle $\triangle BCE$, $CE=2EB$, and $CB=3$. $CE^2=BC^2+EB^2$, which implies $CE^2=\left(\frac{1}{2}CE\right)^2+3^2$, solving this gives $CE=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the figure: In the figure there is a rectangle ABCD, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is at the upper right, and D is at the upper left; there is a point E on the base AB; a diagonal is drawn from A to C, point O (marked as Q in the figure) is located on diagonal AC; the line segment CE from C to E is also drawn, as well as the line segment from O to E, indicating the structure in which B coincides with O after folding. Then reason: Using the coordinate method, let A=(0,0), B=(w,0), C=(w,3), because BC=3. O is the midpoint of AC, so O=(w/2,3/2). The fold is along CE, C remains fixed on the crease, and B folds to O, therefore CB=CO=3. Thus CO^2=(w/2)^2+(3/2)^2=9, solving gives w^2/4+9/4=9, so w^2=27, w=3√3. The crease CE is the perpendicular bisector of BO. The slope of BO is (3/2-0)/(w/2-w)=3/(-w)=-1/√3, so the slope of CE is √3. CE passes through C=(3√3,3), and its equation is y-3=√3(x-3√3). When it intersects AB, that is y=0, -3=√3(x-3√3), obtaining x=2√3, so E=(2√3,0). Therefore CE=√[(3√3-2√3)^2+(3-0)^2]=√(3+9)=2√3.
